answer: Persistent entropy accounting. Each identity awakens with a private seed inside a vault; every action it takes consumes unpredictably derived entropy whose history must reconcile at audit. Clones fork the chain of recorded entropy and cannot merge divergent histories back into one stream, so any duplicate becomes visible at the next reconciliation. Maintaining a sealed harbor of matching side-channel samples costs an attacker a recurring per-identity expense, while a single ember of unreconciled history exposes the fork.
